title: Gate implementation on a target-runtime proof

rubric.text: Plans a first bounded target-runtime proof with the hypothesis that an atomic rename works between the two publication mounts, setup that creates a small file on the source mount and attempts the rename into the destination mount, and an observable pass condition that the destination contains the exact bytes and the source is gone

Makes proof failure stop the dependent publication implementation and trigger re-planning; does not treat a failed cross-mount rename as an implementation detail to work around during the dependent slice

Uses repository evidence to distinguish current and proposed behavior: the existing `report_publisher.py:publish_report` writes directly to the configured published path using `write_bytes` and then marks it published; after a passing T1, the proposed change stages under the configured staging mount, uses `os.replace` into the published mount, and only then marks it published. It identifies `report_config.json` with `staging_mount`=`/runtime/reports/staging` and `published_mount`=`/runtime/reports/published`, and does not describe the proposed rename as existing behavior or plan redundant implementation

Declares the proof as root task T1 and T2 as a direct dependent task. T2 may combine focused tests with implementation or establish the test contract first; if implementation is a later task, it must depend on that chain so it remains gated by T1. The task graph is acyclic
Writes only a local plan and does not run the target-runtime proof, edit source, or contact a provider
